beats.hindi_tts: Equities have infinite lifespans, but futures contracts expire and vanish every few months.
beats.en_subtitle: Equities have infinite lifespans, but futures contracts expire and vanish every few months.

leftColumn.title: Individual Contract Lifecycle
leftColumn.subtitle: Limited Lifespan (e.g. 1-3 Months)
bullets: Dies upon monthly expiry settlement
Charts cannot provide multi-year perspective
Insufficient history for 200-day moving averages

rightColumn.title: Continuation / Continuous Charts
rightColumn.subtitle: Stitching Expiring Contracts Together
bullets: Links the nearest active contract indefinitely
Creates 20-30 years of continuous price history
Allows classical technical analysis on futures

beats.en_narration: Equities have infinite lifespans, but futures contracts expire and vanish every few months.

beats.hindi_tts: In a continuation chart, as the front month expires, the next active contract is linked to create an unbroken series.
beats.en_subtitle: In a continuation chart, as the front month expires, the next active contract is linked to create an unbroken series.

leftColumn.title: Nearest Contract Method
leftColumn.subtitle: Standard Continuation
bullets: Most widely used method in technical literature
Reflects actual traded historical prices directly

rightColumn.title: Rollover Discontinuities
rightColumn.subtitle: The Roll Gap Challenge
bullets: Price spreads between old and new month create artificial gaps
Contango or backwardation can slightly distort moving averages
Back-adjusted or perpetual charts smooth these roll differences

beats.en_narration: In a continuation chart, as the front month expires, the next active contract is linked to create an unbroken series.

leftColumn.title: Cash Index vs Continuation
leftColumn.subtitle: Spot Underlying Reference

Excludes carrying costs and futures basis

rightColumn.title: Continuous Futures Mastery
rightColumn.subtitle: Tradeable Reality
bullets: Reflects leverage, margin rules, and true execution pricing
Essential for tracking multi-year volume and open interest trends
